name: Weather Conditions (Cloud Cover/Rain/Wind)
description: Variable weather significantly impacts image quality. Heavy cloud cover obscures features, requiring more images. Rain creates reflections and reduces visibility, increasing analysis time for both human and onboard systems. Wind affects stability and image sharpness, demanding retakes. This is extremely likely due to the inherent variability of outdoor environments.

name: Lighting Conditions (Sun Angle/Intensity/Shadows)
description: Changes in sun angle dramatically affect contrast and shadow patterns, impacting image interpretability. Low light requires higher resolution or longer exposure times, increasing both human and onboard analysis time.  Sudden changes in light are particularly problematic.

name: Target Object Variability (Size, Shape, Material, Texture)
description: The type of objects being imaged matters.  If the images are predominantly of small, reflective metallic objects, the onboard classifier might struggle more than images of large, textured, non-reflective objects. This is likely to be a consistent factor if the mission involves specific target types.

name: UAV Stability & Gimbal Performance
description: Variations in UAV stability, particularly roll and pitch, introduce motion blur and distortion in the images. This increases the difficulty for both the human operator and the onboard system to accurately interpret features.

name: Operator Fatigue/Experience
description: Human operator performance can fluctuate due to fatigue or varying levels of experience.  This will lead to subjective variations in analysis time.

name: Onboard Classifier Training Data Bias
description: The onboard classifier's training data may not adequately represent the variability of the images it's encountering during the mission.  This can lead to underperformance when faced with unexpected image features.

name: Image Resolution/Sensor Quality
description: Lower image resolution or poor sensor quality introduce noise and detail loss, making analysis more challenging for both the human operator and the onboard system.

name: Time of Day (Sunrise/Sunset)
description: The position of the sun dramatically affects shadows and highlights, impacting image interpretability, leading to variations in analysis times similar to lighting conditions.

name: Terrain Type (Urban, Rural, Forest)
description: The terrain significantly influences the complexity of the scenes being imaged. Urban scenes can have a lot of occlusion and reflective surfaces. Forest scenes can have dense foliage.  Each presents a different challenge.

name: Target Object Movement
description: If the objects of interest are moving, it increases the complexity of the analysis task for both the human and the onboard system, necessitating more images and/or more detailed analysis.

name: UAV Communication Latency
description: Delays in the UAV’s communication with the control system (and therefore the operator) can increase the perceived mission time, particularly if retakes are required.

name: Presence of Reflective Surfaces
description: Significant reflections (water, glass, metal) can confuse both the onboard classifier and human operators, leading to increased analysis time.

name: GPS Signal Quality/Availability
description: Poor GPS signal affects waypoint accuracy, which in turn can impact the quality of the images captured and, thus, analysis time.

name: Sensor Calibration Drift
description: Over time, the UAV's sensors can experience calibration drift, leading to gradual changes in image characteristics (brightness, color balance) which can affect analysis times.

name: Operator Prior Knowledge/Task Complexity
description: The cognitive load associated with the task itself can influence the time taken by the operator. Complex tasks with ambiguous targets will naturally require more time.
